Thus item 2 follows from Lemma C.20 (note that 𝐠t≠0\mathbf{g}_{t}\neq 0 since ‖𝐠t‖⋆≥Ω⁡(ℒ​‖𝜽t‖L−1)>0{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}\geq\Omega(\mathcal{L}\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert^{L-1})>0 by Assumptions (T1),(T2) and Lemma C.2, and therefore 𝐦t,𝐯t≠0\mathbf{m}_{t},\mathbf{v}_{t}\neq 0 by Equations (44),  (45)).

∎

Theorem C.21 (KKT Stationarity for Momentum SD - Implies Theorem 3.3).

Assume 𝛉t\bm{\theta}_{t} follows a trajectory of normalized or unnormalized momentum steepest descent under Assumptions (M1-Weak), (M2), (LR-MSD), (T1), (T2), (T3). Then 𝛉¯=limt→∞𝛉t‖𝛉t‖\bar{\bm{\theta}}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\bm{\theta}_{t}}{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert} is along the direction of a KKT point of the ‖⋅‖\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert-max-margin problem (Equation (11)).

Proof.

We claim that in both the normalized and unnormalized cases it holds that ‖d​𝜽td​t‖≤o⁡(t1L−1)\left\lVert\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert\leq\mathrm{o}\left(t^{\frac{1}{L}-1}\right). In the normalized case this is straightforward since ‖d​θtd​t‖=η⁡(t)≤o⁡(t1L−1)\left\lVert\frac{d\theta_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert=\eta(t)\leq\mathrm{o}\left(t^{\frac{1}{L}-1}\right). In the unnormalized case, by (T1),(T2), it holds that ‖𝐠t‖⋆=Θ⁡(‖𝜽t‖L−1​ℒ){\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}=\Theta(\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert^{L-1}\mathcal{L}) is bounded (Lemma  C.2), so ‖𝐦t‖⋆{\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star} is bounded (Corollary B.6), implying that also in this case ‖d​𝜽td​t‖=η⁡(t)​‖𝐦t‖⋆≤𝒪⁡(η⁡(t))≤o⁡(t1L−1)\left\lVert\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert=\eta(t){\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}\leq\mathcal{O}\left(\eta(t)\right)\leq\mathrm{o}\left(t^{\frac{1}{L}-1}\right).

Note that for any α>0\alpha>0 it holds that

arg⁡min‖𝐮‖=α​⟨𝐮,𝐦t⟩=arg⁡min‖𝐮‖=1​⟨α​𝐮,𝐦t⟩=α​arg​min‖𝐮‖=1​⟨𝐮,𝐦t⟩,\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=\alpha}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle=\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=1}\left\langle\alpha\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle=\alpha\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle~,

so in both the normalized and unnormalized cases, it holds that

d​𝜽td​t‖d​𝜽td​t‖=arg⁡min‖𝐮‖=1​⟨𝐮,𝐦t⟩.\frac{\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}}{\left\lVert\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert}=\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle~.

Thus

⟨d​𝜽td​t‖d​𝜽td​t‖,−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖⋆⟩\displaystyle\left\langle\frac{\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}}{\left\lVert\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert},-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}\right\rangle =⟨arg⁡min‖𝐮‖=1​⟨𝐮,𝐦t⟩,−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖⋆⟩=⟨arg⁡min‖𝐮‖=1​⟨𝐮,𝐦t⟩,−𝐦t‖𝐦t‖⋆+𝐦t‖𝐦t‖⋆−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖⋆⟩\displaystyle=\left\langle\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle,-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}\right\rangle=\left\langle\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle,-\frac{\mathbf{m}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}+\frac{\mathbf{m}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}\right\rangle
=1+⟨arg⁡min‖𝐮‖=1​⟨𝐮,𝐦t⟩,𝐦t‖𝐦t‖⋆−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖⋆⟩.\displaystyle=1+\left\langle\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle,\frac{\mathbf{m}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}\right\rangle~.

We claim that 𝜽t\bm{\theta}_{t} is an approximate steepest descent trajectory (Definition C.12) with ν⁡(t)=‖d​𝜽td​t‖\nu(t)=\left\lVert\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert and Rm​a​x≤1R_{max}\leq 1. We have already seen ‖𝐠t‖⋆≠0{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}\neq 0. By Lemma C.13, it suffices to show that ess​limt→∞⁡⟨d​𝜽tdt‖d​𝜽tdt‖,−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖⋆⟩=1\esslim_{t\to\infty}\left\langle\frac{\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}}{\left\lVert\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert},-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}\right\rangle=1. It therefore suffices to show that

ess​limt→∞⁡⟨arg⁡min‖𝐮‖=1​⟨𝐮,𝐦t⟩,𝐦t‖𝐦t‖⋆−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖⋆⟩=0.\esslim_{t\to\infty}\left\langle\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle,\frac{\mathbf{m}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}\right\rangle=0~.

And since ‖arg⁡min‖𝐮‖=1​⟨𝐮,𝐦t⟩‖=1\left\lVert\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle\right\rVert=1, it suffices to show that

𝐦t‖𝐦t‖⋆−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖⋆​⟶t→∞​0.\frac{\mathbf{m}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}\overset{t\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}0~.

And this is a result of Lemma C.19. Now the KKT result follows from Theorem C.17. ∎

C.6 Composite MSD Algorithms, Muon and Muon-Signum

In this section we prove a simple lemma showing that by partitioning the parameters of a model and training each part with a different normalized SD/MSD algorithm, the resulting algorithm is itself normalized SD/MSD with respect to the maximum among the norms. This allows formulating Muon (on multi-layer networks) and composite algorithms (such as running Muon on matrices and Signum on non-matrix parameters) as normalized momentum steepest descent algorithms.

Lemma C.22 (Dual of Max Norm).

Let 𝛉=(𝐮1,…,𝐮K)\bm{\theta}=\left(\mathbf{u}_{1},...,\mathbf{u}_{K}\right) be a product representation of ℝp\mathbb{R}^{p}, with 𝐮k∈ℝpk,∑kpk=p\mathbf{u}_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{p_{k}},\sum_{k}p_{k}=p. Let {‖⋅‖(k)}k=1K\{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K} be norms on ℝpk\mathbb{R}^{p_{k}} with dual norms {‖⋅‖(k),⋆}k=1K\{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{(k),\star}\}_{k=1}^{K}. Denote ‖𝛉‖=maxk⁡‖𝐮k‖\left\lVert\bm{\theta}\right\rVert=\max_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rVert. Then ‖⋅‖\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert is a norm, and its dual norm is ‖𝛉‖⋆=∑k‖𝐮k‖(k),⋆{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}\right\rVert}_{\star}=\sum_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k),\star}.

Proof.

First, it is a standard result that ‖⋅‖\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert is a norm (one can easily verify that ‖⋅‖\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert satisfies positive definiteness, homogeneity and the triangle inequality). Note that

‖𝜽‖⋆\displaystyle{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}\right\rVert}_{\star} :=max⁡{⟨𝐱,𝜽⟩∣‖𝐱‖=1}\displaystyle:=\max\left\{\left\langle\mathbf{x},\bm{\theta}\right\rangle\mid\left\lVert\mathbf{x}\right\rVert=1\right\}
=max⁡{∑k⟨𝐱k,𝐮k⟩∣maxk⁡‖𝐱k‖(k)=1}\displaystyle=\max\left\{\sum_{k}\left\langle\mathbf{x}_{k},\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rangle\mid\max_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k)}=1\right\}
=max⁡{∑k‖𝐱k‖(k)​‖𝐮k‖(k),⋆∣maxk⁡‖𝐱k‖(k)=1}\displaystyle=\max\left\{\sum_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k)}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k),\star}\mid\max_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k)}=1\right\}
=∑k‖𝐮k‖(k),⋆.\displaystyle=\sum_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k),\star}~.

The third equality holds since for each kk, by definition of the dual norm ⟨𝐱k,𝐮k⟩\left\langle\mathbf{x}_{k},\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rangle is upper bounded by ‖𝐱k‖(k)​‖𝐮k‖(k),⋆\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k)}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k),\star} and this bound is attained by choosing 𝐱k\mathbf{x}_{k} in the direction that defines ‖𝐮k‖(k),⋆\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k),\star}. The last equality holds by choosing ∀k:‖𝐱k‖(k)=1\forall k:\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{k}\right\rVert_{(k)}=1. ∎

Lemma C.23 (Composing SD and MSD Algorithms).

Let 𝛉t=(𝐮1​(t),…,𝐮K​(t))\bm{\theta}_{t}=\left(\mathbf{u}_{1}(t),...,\mathbf{u}_{K}(t)\right) be an arc of parameters of a model f⁡(𝐱i,𝛉t)f(\mathbf{x}_{i};\bm{\theta}_{t}) with 𝐮k∈ℝpk,∑kpk=p\mathbf{u}_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{p_{k}},\sum_{k}p_{k}=p. Denote a choice of subgradients 𝐠t=(𝐠1​(t),…,𝐠K​(t))∈∂ℒ⁡(𝛉t)\mathbf{g}_{t}=(\mathbf{g}_{1}(t),...,\mathbf{g}_{K}(t))\in\partial\mathcal{L}(\bm{\theta}_{t}), and momentum estimates 𝐦t=(𝐦1​(t),…,𝐦K​(t))\mathbf{m}_{t}=(\mathbf{m}_{1}(t),...,\mathbf{m}_{K}(t)). Let {‖⋅‖(k)}k=1K\{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K} be norms on ℝpk\mathbb{R}^{p_{k}} with dual norms {‖⋅‖(k),⋆}k=1K\{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{(k),\star}\}_{k=1}^{K}. Assume there exists η⁡(t)>0\eta(t)>0 so that for all k∈[K]k\in[K] one of the following hold:

  1. 1.

    (Normalized SD) For almost any tt,

    d​𝐮k​(t)d​t∈η⁡(t)​arg⁡min‖𝐮‖(k)=1​⟨𝐮,𝐠k​(t)⟩.\frac{d\mathbf{u}_{k}(t)}{dt}\in\eta(t)\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert_{(k)}=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rangle~.
  2. 2.

    (Normalized MSD) For almost any tt,

    d​𝐮k​(t)d​t∈η⁡(t)​arg⁡min‖𝐮‖(k)=1​⟨𝐮,𝐦k​(t)⟩.\frac{d\mathbf{u}_{k}(t)}{dt}\in\eta(t)\arg\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert_{(k)}=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{k}(t)\right\rangle~.

Then, 𝛉t\bm{\theta}_{t} is a trajectory of normalized SD / normalized MSD respectively, with respect to the norm ‖𝛉‖=maxk⁡‖𝐮k‖\left\lVert\bm{\theta}\right\rVert=\max_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{k}\right\rVert.

Proof.

By definition of the dual norm it holds that

min‖𝐮‖(k)=1⁡⟨𝐮,𝐠k​(t)⟩=−‖𝐠k​(t)‖(k),⋆,min‖𝐮‖(k)=1⁡⟨𝐮,𝐦k​(t)⟩=−‖𝐦k​(t)‖(k),⋆.\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert_{(k)}=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rangle=-\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rVert_{(k),\star},\quad\min_{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert_{(k)}=1}\left\langle\mathbf{u},\mathbf{m}_{k}(t)\right\rangle=-\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{k}(t)\right\rVert_{(k),\star}~.

Therefore in the case of SD, for almost any tt,

⟨1η⁡(t)d​𝜽td​t,𝐠t⟩=∑k⟨1η⁡(t)d​𝐮k​(t)d​t,𝐠k(t)⟩=−∑k‖𝐠k(t)‖(k),⋆=Lemma C.22−‖𝐠t‖⋆.\left\langle\frac{1}{\eta(t)}\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt},\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rangle=\sum_{k}\left\langle\frac{1}{\eta(t)}\frac{d\mathbf{u}_{k}(t)}{dt},\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rangle=-\sum_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rVert_{(k),\star}\overset{\text{Lemma~\ref{lemma:dual_norm_of_max}}}{=}-{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}~.

Similarly in the case of MSD,

⟨1η⁡(t)d​𝜽td​t,𝐦t⟩=∑k⟨1η⁡(t)d​𝐮k​(t)d​t,𝐦k(t)⟩=−∑k‖𝐦k(t)‖(k),⋆=Lemma C.22−‖𝐦t‖⋆.\left\langle\frac{1}{\eta(t)}\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle=\sum_{k}\left\langle\frac{1}{\eta(t)}\frac{d\mathbf{u}_{k}(t)}{dt},\mathbf{m}_{k}(t)\right\rangle=-\sum_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{k}(t)\right\rVert_{(k),\star}\overset{\text{Lemma~\ref{lemma:dual_norm_of_max}}}{=}-{\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}~.

∎

The following is a more general lemma pertaining to approximate SD algorithms.

Lemma C.24 (Composing Approximate SD Algorithms).

Let 𝛉t=(𝐮1​(t),…,𝐮K​(t))\bm{\theta}_{t}=\left(\mathbf{u}_{1}(t),...,\mathbf{u}_{K}(t)\right) be an arc of parameters of a model f⁡(𝐱i,𝛉t)f(\mathbf{x}_{i};\bm{\theta}_{t}) with 𝐮k∈ℝpk,∑kpk=p\mathbf{u}_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{p_{k}},\sum_{k}p_{k}=p. Denote a choice of subgradients 𝐠t=(𝐠1​(t),…,𝐠K​(t))∈∂ℒ⁡(𝛉t)\mathbf{g}_{t}=(\mathbf{g}_{1}(t),...,\mathbf{g}_{K}(t))\in\partial\mathcal{L}(\bm{\theta}_{t}), with eventually 𝐠i​(t)≠𝟎\mathbf{g}_{i}(t)\neq{\mathbf{0}} for almost any tt. Assume there exists ν⁡(t)>0,R1,..,RK>0\nu(t)>0,R_{1},..,R_{K}>0 and norms {‖⋅‖(k)}k=1K\{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K} (with dual norms {‖⋅‖(k),⋆}k=1K\{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{(k),\star}\}_{k=1}^{K}) so that:

  1. 1.

    ∫0tν​⟶t→∞​∞\int_{0}^{t}\nu\overset{t\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}\infty

  2. 2.

    ∀k∈[K]:lim supt→∞‖𝐮k​(t)‖(k)∫0tν≤Rk\forall k\in[K]:\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{k}(t)\right\rVert_{(k)}}{\int_{0}^{t}\nu}\leq R_{k}

  3. 3.

    ∀k∈[K]:ess​liminft→∞⁡rk​(t)≥1\forall k\in[K]:\essliminf_{t\to\infty}r_{k}(t)\geq 1 where rk​(t)​=a.e.​⟨1ν⁡(t)​d​𝐮k​(t)d​t,−𝐠k​(t)‖𝐠k​(t)‖(k),⋆⟩r_{k}(t)\overset{a.e.}{=}\left\langle\frac{1}{\nu(t)}\frac{d\mathbf{u}_{k}(t)}{dt},-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rVert_{(k),\star}}\right\rangle

Then 𝛉t\bm{\theta}_{t} is a trajectory of Approximate Steepest Descent with respect to the norm ‖⋅‖=maxk⁡‖⋅‖(k)\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert=\max_{k}\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{(k)}, ν⁡(t)\nu(t) and Rmax≤maxk⁡RkR_{\text{max}}\leq\max_{k}R_{k}.

Proof.

It clearly holds by definition that lim supt→∞‖𝜽t‖∫0tν≤maxk⁡Rk=Rmax\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert}{\int_{0}^{t}\nu}\leq\max_{k}R_{k}=R_{\text{max}}. Therefore it remains to show ess​liminft→∞⁡r​(t)≥1\essliminf_{t\to\infty}r(t)\geq 1. Indeed, with the same choice of subgradients 𝐠t\mathbf{g}_{t} we have

r⁡(t)=⟨1ν⁡(t)​d​𝜽td​t,−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖⋆⟩=∑k⟨1ν⁡(t)​d​𝐮k​(t)d​t,−𝐠k​(t)⟩∑k‖𝐠k​(t)‖(k),⋆.r(t)=\left\langle\frac{1}{\nu(t)}\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt},-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\star}}\right\rangle=\frac{\sum_{k}\left\langle\frac{1}{\nu(t)}\frac{d\mathbf{u}_{k}(t)}{dt},-\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rangle}{\sum_{k}\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rVert_{(k),\star}}~.

Now note the following general claim: for any set of functions q1​(t),…,qK​(t)q_{1}(t),...,q_{K}(t) and q~1​(t),…,q~K​(t)>0\widetilde{q}_{1}(t),...,\widetilde{q}_{K}(t)>0 with ∀k∈[K]:ess​liminft→∞⁡qkq~k≥1\forall k\in[K]:\essliminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{q_{k}}{\widetilde{q}_{k}}\geq 1 it holds that ess​liminft→∞⁡∑kqk∑kq~k≥1\essliminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\sum_{k}q_{k}}{\sum_{k}\widetilde{q}_{k}}\geq 1. Indeed, for any ε>0\varepsilon>0 it holds eventually for almost any tt that qk​(t)≥q~k​(t)​(1−ε)q_{k}(t)\geq\widetilde{q}_{k}(t)(1-\varepsilon) for all kk, so ∑kqk​(t)≥∑kq~k​(t)​(1−ε)=(1−ε)​∑kq~k​(t)\sum_{k}q_{k}(t)\geq\sum_{k}\widetilde{q}_{k}(t)(1-\varepsilon)=(1-\varepsilon)\sum_{k}\widetilde{q}_{k}(t).

Applying the claim with qk​(t)=⟨1ν⁡(t)​d​𝐮k​(t)d​t,−𝐠k​(t)⟩q_{k}(t)=\left\langle\frac{1}{\nu(t)}\frac{d\mathbf{u}_{k}(t)}{dt},-\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rangle and q~k​(t)=‖𝐠k​(t)‖(k),⋆\widetilde{q}_{k}(t)=\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{k}(t)\right\rVert_{(k),\star} finishes. ∎

Below is our definition of Muon in the exact orthogonalization setting:

Definition C.25 (Spectral and Nuclear Norms).

For a real-valued matrix WW let W=U​Σ​VTW=U\Sigma V^{T} the SVD of WW, for Σ=diag​(σ1,…,σr)\Sigma=\text{diag}(\sigma_{1},...,\sigma_{r}), σi>0\sigma_{i}>0. We denote the spectral and nuclear norms of WW respectively as

‖W‖sp=maxi∈[r]⁡σi,‖W‖nuc=∑i∈[r]σi.{\left\lVert W\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{sp}}=\max_{i\in[r]}\sigma_{i},\quad{\left\lVert W\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{nuc}}=\sum_{i\in[r]}\sigma_{i}~.

For a collection of matrices 𝐖=(W1,…,WK)\mathbf{W}=(W_{1},...,W_{K}) we denote (msp short for max-sp, snuc short for sum-nuc)

‖𝐖‖msp=maxk∈[K]⁡‖Wk‖sp,‖𝐖‖snuc=∑k∈[K]‖Wk‖nuc.{\left\lVert\mathbf{W}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}}=\max_{k\in[K]}{\left\lVert W_{k}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{sp}},\quad{\left\lVert\mathbf{W}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{snuc}}=\sum_{k\in[K]}{\left\lVert W_{k}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{nuc}}~.

It is a standard fact that ‖⋅‖nuc{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{nuc}} is the dual norm of ‖⋅‖sp{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{sp}}. By Lemma C.22 this implies that ‖⋅‖snuc{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{snuc}} is the dual norm of ‖⋅‖msp{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}}.

Definition C.26 (Muon).

Let 𝜽t=(W1​(t),…,WK​(t))∈ℝp\bm{\theta}_{t}=(W_{1}(t),...,W_{K}(t))\in\mathbb{R}^{p} be a trajectory representing a collection of matrices, 𝐠t=(G1​(t),…,GK​(t))∈∂ℒ⁡(𝜽t)\mathbf{g}_{t}=(G_{1}(t),...,G_{K}(t))\in\partial\mathcal{L}(\bm{\theta}_{t}) a choice of subgradients and 𝐦t=(M1​(t),…,MK​(t))\mathbf{m}_{t}=(M_{1}(t),...,M_{K}(t)) a momentum estimate of 𝐠t\mathbf{g}_{t} with parameter c1>0c_{1}>0. The Muon update is defined as d​𝜽td​t=(d​W1d​t,…,d​WKd​t)\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}=(\frac{dW_{1}}{dt},...,\frac{dW_{K}}{dt}) for:

∀k∈[K]:d​Wkd​t∈{−η(t)⋅Uk(t)VkT(t)∣Mk(t)=SVDUk(t)Σk(t)VkT(t)},\forall k\in[K]:\frac{dW_{k}}{dt}\in\left\{-\eta(t)\cdot U_{k}(t)V_{k}^{T}(t)\mid M_{k}(t)\overset{\text{SVD}}{=}U_{k}(t)\Sigma_{k}(t)V_{k}^{T}(t)\right\}~,

where SVD is the reduced SVD operator, i.e. Σk​(t)\Sigma_{k}(t) is a square diagonal matrix with strictly positive diagonal entries and Uk​(t),Vk​(t)U_{k}(t),V_{k}(t) have orthonormal columns.

Lemma C.27.

Muon is a normalized momentum steepest descent algorithm with ‖⋅‖=‖⋅‖msp\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert={\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}}.

Proof.

By the definition of normalized momentum steepest descent, we need to prove that

‖1η⁡(t)​d​𝜽td​t‖msp=1,⟨1η⁡(t)​d​𝜽td​t,𝐦t⟩=−‖𝐦t‖snuc.{\left\lVert\frac{1}{\eta(t)}\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}}=1,\quad\left\langle\frac{1}{\eta(t)}\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt},\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rangle=-{\left\lVert\mathbf{m}_{t}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{snuc}}~.

By definition of these norms, it suffices to show for every kk that (omitting tt for brevity) ‖Uk​Vk⊤‖sp=1{\left\lVert U_{k}V_{k}^{\top}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{sp}}=1 and ⟨Uk​Vk⊤,Mk⟩=‖Mk‖nuc\left\langle U_{k}V_{k}^{\top},M_{k}\right\rangle={\left\lVert M_{k}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{nuc}}. Indeed, ‖Uk​Vk⊤‖sp=1{\left\lVert U_{k}V_{k}^{\top}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{sp}}=1 by definition (Uk​Vk⊤U_{k}V_{k}^{\top} is an SVD of itself with singular values in {1,0}\{1,0\}). Denote Σk=diag​(σ1,…,σr)\Sigma_{k}=\text{diag}(\sigma_{1},...,\sigma_{r}) then we must show

⟨Uk​Vk⊤,Mk⟩=∑i=1rσi.\left\langle U_{k}V_{k}^{\top},M_{k}\right\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\sigma_{i}~.

And indeed, since the elementwise dot product between two matrices X,YX,Y is equal to Tr[X⊤​Y]\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}[X^{\top}Y], using Uk⊤​Uk=I,Vk⊤​Vk=IU_{k}^{\top}U_{k}=I,V_{k}^{\top}V_{k}=I we get

⟨Uk​Vk⊤,Mk⟩=Tr[Mk⊤​Uk​Vk⊤]=Tr[Vk​Σk⊤​Uk⊤​Uk​Vk⊤]=Tr[Vk​Σk⊤​Vk⊤]=Tr[Vk⊤​Vk​Σk⊤]=Tr[Σk⊤]=∑i=1rσi\left\langle U_{k}V_{k}^{\top},M_{k}\right\rangle=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}[M_{k}^{\top}U_{k}V_{k}^{\top}]=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}[V_{k}\Sigma_{k}^{\top}U_{k}^{\top}U_{k}V_{k}^{\top}]=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}[V_{k}\Sigma_{k}^{\top}V_{k}^{\top}]=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}[V_{k}^{\top}V_{k}\Sigma_{k}^{\top}]=\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}[\Sigma_{k}^{\top}]=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\sigma_{i}

∎

Corollary C.28 (KKT Stationarity for Muon - Implies Corollary 3.4).

Assume 𝛉=(W1,…,WK)∈ℝp\bm{\theta}=(W_{1},...,W_{K})\in\mathbb{R}^{p} is a parameter vector representing a collection of matrices, following a trajectory of Muon with a shared learning rate schedule η⁡(t)\eta(t) under Assumptions (M1-Weak), (M2), (LR-MSD), (T1), (T2), (T3). Then 𝛉¯=limt→∞𝛉t‖𝛉t‖\bar{\bm{\theta}}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\bm{\theta}_{t}}{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert} is along the direction of a KKT point of the ‖⋅‖\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert-max-margin problem (Equation (11)), with ‖⋅‖=‖⋅‖msp\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert={\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}}.

Proof.

Follows from Theorem C.21 since 𝜽t\bm{\theta}_{t} is a trajectory of normalized momentum steepest descent with ‖⋅‖=‖⋅‖msp\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert={\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}} (by Lemmas C.23, C.27). ∎

Notice that Lemma C.23 reveals that any collection of momentum steepest descent algorithms may be run in parallel, resulting in a new momentum steepest descent algorithm with respect to the maximal norm. In particular, Muon-Signum, i.e. running Muon on weight matrices and Signum on non-matrix parameters, answers this definition.

Corollary C.29 (KKT Stationarity for Muon-Signum - Implies Corollary 3.5).

Assume 𝛉=(W1,…,WK,𝐮)=(𝐖,𝐮)∈ℝp\bm{\theta}=(W_{1},...,W_{K},\mathbf{u})=(\mathbf{W},\mathbf{u})\in\mathbb{R}^{p} is a parameter vector representing a collection of matrices and additional parameters 𝐮\mathbf{u}. Assume W1,…,WKW_{1},...,W_{K} follow a trajectory of Muon and 𝐮\mathbf{u} follows a trajectory of Signum, with a shared scheduled learning rate η⁡(t)\eta(t). Assume (M1-Weak), (M2), (LR-MSD), (T1), (T2), (T3). Then 𝛉¯=limt→∞𝛉t‖𝛉t‖\bar{\bm{\theta}}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\bm{\theta}_{t}}{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert} is along the direction of a KKT point of the ‖⋅‖\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert-max-margin problem (Equation (11)), with ‖𝛉‖=max⁡{‖𝐖‖msp,‖𝐮‖∞}\left\lVert\bm{\theta}\right\rVert=\max\{{\left\lVert\mathbf{W}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}},\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert_{\infty}\}.

Proof.

Follows from Theorem C.21 since 𝜽t\bm{\theta}_{t} is a trajectory of normalized momentum steepest descent with ‖𝜽‖=max⁡{‖𝐖‖msp,‖𝐮‖∞}\left\lVert\bm{\theta}\right\rVert=\max\{{\left\lVert\mathbf{W}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}},\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert_{\infty}\} (by Lemmas C.23, C.27). ∎

C.7 Adam

In this section we show that Adam is an approximate steepest descent algorithm with ‖⋅‖=‖⋅‖∞\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert=\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{\infty} in the regime of a non-increasing learning rate η⁡(t)≤o⁡(t1L−1),∫0∞η=∞\eta(t)\leq\mathrm{o}\left(t^{\frac{1}{L}-1}\right),\int_{0}^{\infty}\eta=\infty (i.e. (LR-Adam)). This allows us to infer using Theorem C.17 that the assumed directional limit point 𝜽¯=limt→∞𝜽t‖𝜽t‖\bar{\bm{\theta}}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\bm{\theta}_{t}}{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert} of the trajectory is the direction of a KKT point of the ℓ∞\ell_{\infty}-max-margin problem. Recall again that (T3) is implied by (T2) if strengthening (M1-Weak) to (M1).

Theorem C.30 (KKT Stationarity for Adam - Implies Theorem 3.6).

Let 𝛉t\bm{\theta}_{t} be a trajectory of Adam with c1≥c2c_{1}\geq c_{2} (Equation (8)), under Assumptions (M1-Weak), (M2), (LR-Adam), (T1), (T2), (T3), (A1). Then the limit point 𝛉¯\bar{\bm{\theta}} of 𝛉t‖𝛉t‖\frac{\bm{\theta}_{t}}{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert} is the direction of a KKT point of Problem (11) with ‖⋅‖=‖⋅‖∞\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert=\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{\infty}.

Proof.

First, by assumptions (T1), (T2), it holds (Lemma  C.2) that ‖𝐠t‖1=Θ⁡(‖𝜽t‖L−1​ℒ)\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}=\Theta(\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert^{L-1}\mathcal{L}) and in particular eventually 𝐠t≠𝟎\mathbf{g}_{t}\neq{\mathbf{0}}. By Lemma B.4, denote C=C⁡(c1,c2)>0C=C(c_{1},c_{2})>0 with ∀t:‖𝐦t𝐯t‖∞≤C\forall t:\left\lVert\frac{\mathbf{m}_{t}}{\sqrt{\mathbf{v}_{t}}}\right\rVert_{\infty}\leq C. This and (LR-Adam) imply that ‖d​𝜽td​t‖≤o⁡(t1L−1)\left\lVert\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt}\right\rVert\leq\mathrm{o}\left(t^{\frac{1}{L}-1}\right). Therefore by Lemma C.19 with ‖⋅‖=‖⋅‖∞\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert=\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{\infty}, fixing ε>0\varepsilon>0, there exist ej​(t),ej′​(t)​⟶t→∞​0e_{j}(t),e_{j}^{\prime}(t)\overset{t\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}0 with:

∀j∈Jε​(t):𝐦t​[j]=𝐠t​[j]​(1+ej​(t)),𝐯t​[j]=|𝐠t​[j]|​(1+ej′​(t)).\forall j\in J_{\varepsilon}(t):\quad\quad\mathbf{m}_{t}[j]=\mathbf{g}_{t}[j](1+e_{j}(t)),\quad\sqrt{\mathbf{v}_{t}[j]}=\left|\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]\right|(1+e_{j}^{\prime}(t))~.

Recalling 𝐦^t=(1−e−c1​t)−1​𝐦t,𝐯^t=(1−e−c2​t)−1​𝐯t\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}=(1-e^{-c_{1}t})^{-1}\mathbf{m}_{t},\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}=(1-e^{-c_{2}t})^{-1}\mathbf{v}_{t}, since the bias correction terms themselves tend to 1 there exist ej​(t)​⟶t→∞​0e_{j}(t)\overset{t\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}0 with (reusing the notation eje_{j})

∀j∈Jε​(t):𝐦^t​[j]𝐯^t​[j]=sign⁡(𝐠t​[j])⋅(1+ej​(t)).\forall j\in J_{\varepsilon}(t):\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}[j]}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}}[j]}=\mathrm{sign}\left(\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]\right)\cdot(1+e_{j}(t))~.

Again since 1−e−c2​t1−e−c1​t→1\frac{\sqrt{1-e^{-c_{2}t}}}{1-e^{-c_{1}t}}\to 1 there exists t1≥0t_{1}\geq 0 with ∀t≥t1:2​C≥‖𝐦^t𝐯^t‖∞\forall t\geq t_{1}:2C\geq\left\lVert\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}}}\right\rVert_{\infty}. Denote C^:=max⁡{2​C,supt∈(0,t1]‖𝐦^t𝐯^t‖∞}\hat{C}:=\max\left\{2C,\sup_{t\in(0,t_{1}]}\left\lVert\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}}}\right\rVert_{\infty}\right\} an upper bound on ‖𝐦^t𝐯^t‖∞\left\lVert\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}}}\right\rVert_{\infty} for all t>0t>0 (the supremum is finite by Lemma B.9). For any j∉Jε​(t)j\notin J_{\varepsilon}(t) it holds that |𝐦^t​[j]𝐯^t​[j]​𝐠t​[j]‖𝐠t‖1|≤ε​C^\left|\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}[j]}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}[j]}}\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}}\right|\leq\varepsilon\hat{C}. Also, ∑j∈Jε​(t)|𝐠t​[j]|≥∑j∈[p]|𝐠t​[j]|−ε​p​‖𝐠t‖1=‖𝐠t‖1​(1−ε​p)\sum_{j\in J_{\varepsilon}(t)}\left|\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]\right|\geq\sum_{j\in[p]}\left|\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]\right|-\varepsilon p\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}=\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}(1-\varepsilon p). Therefore,

⟨𝐦^t𝐯^t,𝐠t‖𝐠t‖1⟩\displaystyle\left\langle\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}}},\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}}\right\rangle ≥∑j∈Jε​(t)𝐦^t​[j]𝐯^t​[j]​𝐠t​[j]‖𝐠t‖1−ε​C^​p=∑j∈Jε​(t)(1+ej​(t))​sign⁡(𝐠t​[j])​𝐠t​[j]‖𝐠t‖1−ε​C^​p\displaystyle\geq\sum_{j\in J_{\varepsilon}(t)}\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}[j]}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}}[j]}\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}}-\varepsilon\hat{C}p=\sum_{j\in J_{\varepsilon}(t)}(1+e_{j}(t))\frac{\mathrm{sign}\left(\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]\right)\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}}-\varepsilon\hat{C}p
≥minj⁡(1+ej​(t))⋅∑j∈Jε​(t)|𝐠t​[j]|‖𝐠t‖1−ε​C^​p\displaystyle\geq\min_{j}(1+e_{j}(t))\cdot\frac{\sum_{j\in J_{\varepsilon}(t)}\left|\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]\right|}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}}-\varepsilon\hat{C}p
≥minj⁡(1+ej​(t))⋅‖𝐠t‖1​(1−ε​p)‖𝐠t‖1−ε​C^​p\displaystyle\geq\min_{j}(1+e_{j}(t))\cdot\frac{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}(1-\varepsilon p)}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}}-\varepsilon\hat{C}p
⟶t→∞​1−ε​p−ε​C^​p.\displaystyle\overset{t\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}1-\varepsilon p-\varepsilon\hat{C}p~.

Since this holds for any ε>0\varepsilon>0, this implies

lim inft→∞⟨𝐦^t𝐯^t,𝐠t‖𝐠t‖1⟩≥1.\liminf_{t\to\infty}\left\langle\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{t}}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{t}}},\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}}\right\rangle\geq 1~.

Therefore,

liminft→∞⟨1η⁡(t)​d​𝜽td​t,−𝐠t‖𝐠t‖1⟩≥1.\lim\inf_{t\to\infty}\left\langle\frac{1}{\eta(t)}\frac{d\bm{\theta}_{t}}{dt},-\frac{\mathbf{g}_{t}}{\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{t}\right\rVert_{1}}\right\rangle\geq 1~.

Also, since ‖𝜽t‖∞≤∫0tη⁡(s)​‖𝐦^s𝐯^s‖∞​𝑑s≤C^​∫0tη⁡(s)​𝑑s\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert_{\infty}\leq\int_{0}^{t}\eta(s)\left\lVert\frac{\hat{\mathbf{m}}_{s}}{\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{s}}}\right\rVert_{\infty}ds\leq\hat{C}\int_{0}^{t}\eta(s)ds it holds that

lim supt→∞‖𝜽t‖∞∫0tη≤C^.\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert_{\infty}}{\int_{0}^{t}\eta}\leq\hat{C}~.

Therefore, by Lemma C.15, ℒ⁡(𝜽t)→0,‖𝜽t‖→∞\mathcal{L}(\bm{\theta}_{t})\to 0,\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert\to\infty. This in turn implies that ∀j∈[p]:|𝐠t​[j]|​⟶t→∞​0\forall j\in[p]:\left|\mathbf{g}_{t}[j]\right|\overset{t\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}0 (by Equation (25), noting that ‖𝜽t‖L−1=o⁡(ℒ−1)\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert^{L-1}=\mathrm{o}\left(\mathcal{L}^{-1}\right)), so by Lemma B.10 it follows that in fact

limsupt→∞‖𝜽t‖∞∫0tη≤1.\lim\sup_{t\to\infty}\frac{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert_{\infty}}{\int_{0}^{t}\eta}\leq 1~.

C.8 Muon-Adam

Muon-Adam differs from Muon-Signum in that it does not adhere to the definition of normalized momentum steepest descent (due to the presence of Adam). Therefore the treatment of Muon-Adam relies directly on the framework of Approximate Steepest Descent, drawing main techniques from both Theorem C.30 and Theorem C.21. In addition to those, the key technical step is dividing [0,∞)[0,\infty) into times tt when the dual norm has a significant contribution from the ‖⋅‖1\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_{1} norm of the gradient w.r.t 𝐮\mathbf{u}, and times when there is a significant contribution from the ‖⋅‖snuc{\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{snuc}} norm of the gradient w.r.t 𝐖\mathbf{W} (these subsets may overlap).

Theorem C.31 (KKT Stationarity for Muon-Adam - Implies Theorem 3.7).

Assume 𝛉=(W1,…,WK,𝐮)=(𝐖,𝐮)∈ℝp\bm{\theta}=(W_{1},...,W_{K},\mathbf{u})=(\mathbf{W},\mathbf{u})\in\mathbb{R}^{p} is a parameter vector representing a collection of matrices and additional parameters 𝐮\mathbf{u}. Assume W1,…,WKW_{1},...,W_{K} follow a trajectory of Muon and 𝐮\mathbf{u} follows a trajectory of Adam, with respective learning rates of the form η0M​η​(t),η0A​η​(t)\eta_{0}^{M}\eta(t),\eta_{0}^{A}\eta(t) for η0M,η0A>0\eta_{0}^{M},\eta_{0}^{A}>0 and momentum parameters cMc_{M} for Muon and c1≥c2c_{1}\geq c_{2} for Adam. Assume (M1-Weak), (M2), (LR-Adam), (T1), (T2), (T3), (A1). Then 𝛉¯=limt→∞𝛉t‖𝛉t‖\bar{\bm{\theta}}=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\bm{\theta}_{t}}{\left\lVert\bm{\theta}_{t}\right\rVert} is along the direction of a KKT point of the ‖⋅‖\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert-max-margin problem (Equation (11)), with

‖𝜽‖=max⁡{η0Aη0M​‖𝐖‖msp,‖𝐮‖∞}.\left\lVert\bm{\theta}\right\rVert=\max\left\{\frac{\eta_{0}^{A}}{\eta_{0}^{M}}{\left\lVert\mathbf{W}\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}},\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert_{\infty}\right\}~.
Proof.

Appendix D Experimental Details

As mentioned in Section 6, we train two-layer (one hidden layer) homogeneous networks to classify m=2048m=2048 MNIST digits (LeCun et al., 2002) as even or odd, using the exponential loss. We compare squared ReLU and ReLU, and the following optimizers: Normalized Gradient Descent (NGD) with and without momentum, Signum, Adam, Muon (treating the output layer as a matrix with a single row) and Muon-Adam. Training proceeds until the loss reaches a small target value (10−810^{-8}). The stability constant for Adam was chosen to be negligible with respect to gradient norm values (ε=10−20\varepsilon=10^{-20}).

Adam momentum parameters are default (β1=0.9,β2=0.999\beta_{1}=0.9,\beta_{2}=0.999) and momentum for other optimizers is also β=0.9\beta=0.9. Network parameters are initialized using Kaiming (He et al., 2015), with no corrections for non-linearities, and multiplied by a uniform factor α=0.01\alpha=0.01. Initial learning rate values η0\eta_{0} are tuned per-setting to allow for gradual convergence to the target loss value, according to Table 1.

Figure 2 presents results for Muon-Adam (the main results are shown in Figure 1). We observe that compared to Muon and Adam, Muon-Adam maximizes the norm max⁡{‖W‖msp,‖𝐮‖∞}\max\{{\left\lVert W\right\rVert}_{\mathrm{msp}},\left\lVert\mathbf{u}\right\rVert_{\infty}\} as expected, where the matrix WW is the first layer and the vector 𝐮\mathbf{u} is the output layer.
